ProjectWeave request for the selected Task (data):
{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZiHufg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDI8qs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 71, "title": "Resolve and implement sample-level S-DSP FIR filtering and echo feedback arithmetic", "body": "## Problem

The current echo path lacks a reconciled hardware arithmetic contract and meaningful nonzero-FIR regression coverage. This is the next target identified in `latest_assessment`; the supplied context lists no open Issue duplicating it.

At baseline `9b3a7403f440f709593ff9288eb19cf4c8806a56`, [`Dsp::sample`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9b3a7403f440f709593ff9288eb19cf4c8806a56/crates/snes-core/src/dsp.rs#L249-L290):

- Stores full signed RAM words in FIR history and associates coefficient 0 with the newest word.
- Shifts each coefficient product by seven and accumulates all eight terms in `i32`, without intermediate narrowing.
- Clamps feedback and final PCM, and writes feedback without explicitly clearing any low bit.

These are implementation observations, not verified hardware semantics. Existing [noise/echo vectors](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9b3a7403f440f709593ff9288eb19cf4c8806a56/crates/snes-core/src/dsp_noise_tests.rs#L148-L194) use zero FIR/feedback. Their [validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9b3a7403f440f709593ff9288eb19cf4c8806a56/docs/issue-15-validation.md#L70-L75) explicitly disclaims echo saturation coverage.

Incorrect tap order, rounding or intermediate widths can change ordinary audio even when all existing tests pass.

## Expected outcome

Correct the sample-level FIR and feedback path for fixed ESA/EDL settings, using a documented numerical contract and independent executable vectors. This Issue requires an implementation correction, supported by specification reconciliation and tests.

Use the specification references already recorded by the repository:

- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm): S-DSP echo/FIR descriptions and FIR coefficients, EFB, EVOL, EON, ESA, EDL and FLG register entries.
- [Anomie's S-DSP Doc, jwdonal revision 1212](https://gist.github.com/nyanpasu64/a0d916ce6924912a7116682bf778e9a0): SOUND GENERATION, echo processing and associated register descriptions.

**Unresolved planning prerequisite:** the repository does not contain the complete echo specification text or a reconciled arithmetic derivation. External references were not opened under this evaluation's repository-only restriction. Consequently, exact history orientation, intermediate widths, shifts, narrowing and writeback-bit rules remain unresolved here. Do not treat the current code or an earlier Issue contract as the authority.

Before changing expectations, record a source-cited, executable mathematical contract specifying:

1. Signed RAM input interpretation, any input scaling, and the mapping of all eight coefficients to history ages.
2. Signed coefficient multiplication, every arithmetic shift and negative-rounding rule, accumulation order, intermediate wrap/narrowing points and saturation boundaries.
3. FIR-result bit masking; signed EFB feedback arithmetic; feedback-addition narrowing/saturation; and final RAM writeback bits.
4. Signed echo-volume arithmetic and its contribution to final PCM.
5. Write-disable versus output-mute behavior: precisely which RAM writes, filtering, feedback, history and address progression continue.

Cite exact source sections and distinguish agreement, disagreement and emulator conventions. Correct unsupported historical expectations with evidence rather than preserving them because they pass. Do not claim unresolved rules verified.

Scope is the FIR history/filter result and its feedback, RAM-write and PCM consumers at the existing sample boundary. Keep voice-send inputs within independently established ranges to isolate this correction. Do not expand into a general voice-mixer rewrite.

Remaining work includes live ESA/EDL sampling, DSP subcycle register/RAM races, SPC bus synchronization, physical startup/reset retention, and comprehensive multi-voice dry/send saturation. This Issue does not complete `dsp-echo` or `dsp-timing`.

## Context and reproduction

A source-derived current-behavior probe can isolate tap orientation without BRR, envelopes or CPU timing:

1. Construct `Dsp::default()` and zeroed 64 KiB RAM.
2. Set FLG=`$20`, ESA=`$60`, EDL=`1`, EVOLL=`$40`, and FIR coefficients 0–7 to `1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8`.
3. Put the little-endian left impulse `$4000` at `$6000`; leave subsequent frames and the right channel zero.
4. Call `sample` nine times.

Reading the current implementation predicts left PCM `64,128,192,256,320,384,448,512,0`. This probe was not executed during planning and is not a hardware oracle. Derive the required sequence independently from the reconciled specification.

Also inspect the existing noise vector with envelope sample `2` and left voice volume `127`: its zero-FIR RAM assertion currently expects `1`. Reconcile that expectation against the documented echo writeback-bit rule. Preserve its separate source, ENVX, OUTX and dry-PCM assertions unless evidence independently requires a correction.

Existing uploaded-guest patterns are available in [`tests/dsp_noise.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9b3a7403f440f709593ff9288eb19cf4c8806a56/crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_noise.rs); [`Apu::tick`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/9b3a7403f440f709593ff9288eb19cf4c8806a56/crates/snes-core/src/apu.rs#L107-L157) provides the existing sample cadence. No scheduler redesign or firmware is needed.

Planning inspected source and guidance read-only; no tests were rerun or files changed.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the exact arithmetic contract above, with source-section citations and worked numerical examples. Resolve discrepancies before establishing golden results. If evidence cannot resolve a required rule, report that prerequisite explicitly rather than inventing a hardware requirement or claiming completion.
- [ ] Implement the supported corrections in the production echo path. Provide baseline-failure/fixed-pass evidence for at least one independently derived nonzero-FIR counterexample. Documentation or tests alone do not complete this Issue.
- [ ] Add focused original unit vectors covering every tap individually, asymmetric multi-tap impulses through history wrap, distinct left/right inputs, signed coefficient endpoints, odd positive/negative inputs, and negative rounding. Assert literal intermediate/final values derived without production helpers or constants.
- [ ] Add overflow discriminators separating the resolved intermediate wrap/saturation behavior from unrestricted `i32` accumulation and final-only clamping. Include both signs and a nonzero final tap. Check numerical PCM and RAM bytes, not only bounds or non-silence.
- [ ] Add nonzero positive/negative EFB sequences with literal expected RAM words over multiple feedback recurrences, including saturation, writeback low bits, echo-only PCM and dry-plus-echo composition. Test zero FIR/EFB/EON controls, write-disable, output mute, history continuity, fixed EDL=0/nonzero delay, and 16-bit RAM-address wrap. Keep live ESA/EDL changes outside these claims.
- [ ] Add an original uploaded SPC700 guest in `crates/snes-core/tests/dsp_echo.rs`. It must configure the DSP through executed `$F2/$F3` writes and produce a nonzero-FIR, nonzero-feedback sequence. Assert independent numeric PCM and guest-recorded echo RAM results, bounded acknowledgements/execution and no core error. The host may upload original code/data and issue commands; it must not inject private FIR history or expected results. Record authorship, license and build/data provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`; acquire no commercial ROM, firmware or external binary.
- [ ] Compare every PCM sample, DSP registers and echo RAM between whole and irregularly partitioned `Apu::tick` advances through history and delay-buffer wraps. Retain the established cadence checks.
- [ ] Preserve existing envelope, noise, pitch, controller, DMA/HDMA and cleared-game regressions. Any changed historical echo expectation needs a cited hardware correction and before/after evidence; do not weaken unrelated assertions, replay durations, fixture hashes or provenance gates.
- [ ] Run and record the following before merge, using the documented toolchain prerequisites:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --lib dsp::echo_tests
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test dsp_echo
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py \
  --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

The browser gate must retain both cleared five-minute game checks, Castle's complete route, and Memory's numerical music/effect and Web Audio checks. Report failures, skipped checks and toolchain substitutions accurately. Use only original or provenance-approved source-built fixtures.

- [ ] Update README limitations and the validation record. Retain all 24 inventory categories and their scope: 21 partial, `dsp-voices` implemented_unverified, `ppu-raster` and `pal` unimplemented, none verified. Add the selected evidence and specific remaining echo limitations. Limited passing suites establish neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional independently derived FIR coefficient sets and feedback sequences. No subjective listening or physical-device approval is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
